reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read "came no more" in 1 Samuel 7:13 as no lasting Philistine victory during Samuel's life, since the next clause implies renewed but failed attempts.

discrepancy.note: Spinoza notes chapter 7 crushes the Philistines for Samuel's lifetime while chapter 13 has them invading and reducing Israel during that same lifetime.

quotes.text: At the end of chap. vii. it is narrated that the Philistines were so crushed by the Hebrews that they did not venture, during Samuel's life, to invade the borders of Israel; but in chap. xiii. we are told that the Hebrews were invaded during the life of Samuel by the Philistines, and reduced by them to such a state of wretchedness and poverty
quotes.attr: Benedict de Spinoza (d. 1677), A Theologico-Political Treatise, Part II (1883), ch. X, on 1 Samuel 7:13 and 1 Samuel 13:5.

sides.snippet: the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more within the border of Israel
sides.verseText: So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more within the border of Israel: and the hand of Yahweh was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

sides.snippet: The Philistines assembled themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen
sides.verseText: The Philistines assembled themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea-shore in multitude: and they came up, and encamped in Michmash, eastward of Beth Aven.
